newsitem.title: CUBA: 3 provinces meet target in Cuban sugar harvest.
newsitem.headline: 3 provinces meet target in Cuban sugar harvest.

text.p: Cuba's eastern province of Holguin, the only area still milling in the nearly completed 1996-97 sugar cane harvest, became the third province to complete its production target, official media said Thursday.
Communist Party daily Granma said the only other provinces to complete their target in what has been a poorer-than-expected harvest were Santiago de Cuba and Las Tunas, also in the east.
Granma said three mills would continue milling in Holguin following completion of the provincial target Wednesday.
No official estimate has been given for the total expected production in the harvest, which is likely to end in the coming days.
However, the figure is expected to be around 4.1 million to 4.2 million tonnes.
This compares to official forecasts at the start of the harvest last December for a slight improvement on the 1995-96 harvest of 4.45 million tonnes.

Officials have blamed the setback on delays in the arrival of foreign financing for inputs to the harvest, and also the damage caused to cane by a hurricane that swept central and western areas of the island last October.
